trust_decision.summary: Whether a hardened stock-JDK parser must refuse every external resource an xi:include href names is decided by the deny-all entity resolver installed on each DocumentBuilder / XMLReader (StockJdkProvider DOM and SAX recipes), not by the ACCESS_EXTERNAL_* attributes the JDK's XInclude processor ignores.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the stock JDK provider and XInclude, and the only public XInclude promise is XmlFactories.java:192-194 ('XInclude resolution is disabled'); the recipe that has to keep that promise is configure(DocumentBuilderFactory), whose only external-access defence is the ACCESS_EXTERNAL_* pair at lines 70-72.

fix_sites.module_kind: internal provider hardening recipe (non-public), reached through a lower-level public API

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/main/java/eu/copernik/xml/factory/HardeningDocumentBuilderFactory.java:20-30 and src/main/java/eu/copernik/xml/factory/HardeningXMLReader.java:22-45 (already composed by XercesProvider.java:99,123 and AndroidProvider.java:154, not by StockJdkProvider)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The resolver-floor wrappers are documented as the answer for providers that cannot honour ACCESS_EXTERNAL_* (XercesProvider.java:98,122); the stock JDK recipe already sets ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA to "" as a system-property-proof defence (StockJdkProvider.java:70-72, 92-94), so a solver can argue the stock path needs no resolver and that the XInclude string is a documentation bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A caller-installed EntityResolver that allow-lists one specific href must still resolve it, and a DOCTYPE-only document must still parse quietly; only unresolved lookups may throw. Installing Resolvers.DenyAll (the pattern used on the StAX line) breaks both, and the tests asserting them are already in the pinned tree.

O6_input_shapes: DOM path: DocumentBuilder.parse(File) on a factory with setXIncludeAware(true), default and namespace-aware
SAX path: XMLReader.parse(absolute path) on a parser from a factory with setXIncludeAware(true)
href allow-listed by a caller resolver vs not allow-listed

O7_producer.where: src/main/java/eu/copernik/xml/factory/DelegatingSAXParser.java:20-21 with DelegatingSAXParser.java:47-50: SAXParser.parse(source, DefaultHandler) installs the handler as the reader's entity resolver, silently replacing a plain floor installed in configure(XMLReader)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Return new HardeningDocumentBuilderFactory(factory) from a second provider's DOM recipe
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same one-line composition already exists for Xerces at the pinned commit, so a maintainer copying the stock-JDK fix into a sibling provider (or the reverse) is the natural next commit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: AndroidProvider's DOM recipe returns the raw factory while its SAX recipe wraps the reader
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: An asymmetric provider recipe is exactly where a maintainer would later add a HardeningDocumentBuilderFactory for symmetry, even though kxml2 DOM has no XInclude.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Wrap a caller-supplied SAXSource whose XMLReader is a raw stock-JDK reader instead of trusting it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already rewrites every StreamSource through XmlFactories.harden(Source); extending that to a plain reader is the obvious hardening follow-up its own Javadoc caveat hints at.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Route XMLSchemaLoader's internally provisioned reader through a HardeningXMLReader as well as the ACCESS_EXTERNAL_* properties
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The second fix commit's own comment says the resolver floor 'does not reach' the schema/XSLTC compile paths, which invites a maintainer to close exactly that gap.

O9_family: XML external entity / external resource resolution (XXE, CWE-611) via XInclude href
